youtube.title: gRPC over WebRTC DataChannels — No HTTP/2, No Dependencies | grpc-over-datachannels
youtube.description:
grpc-over-datachannels runs gRPC over a single WebRTC RTCDataChannel instead of HTTP/2. Generated, dependency-free runtimes for 16 languages — browser and native — plus WebRTC-Direct examples with direct, TURN, and STUN modes.

Code: https://github.com/browser-grpc/grpc-over-datachannels
In-browser stub generator: https://browser-grpc.github.io/grpc-over-datachannels/app/
Blog: https://c100k.blogspot.com/2026/10/introducing-grpc-over-datachannels-grpc.html

Built with Fish Audio

scenes.heading: gRPC over WebRTC
scenes.sub: One DataChannel. No HTTP/2. No dependencies.
scenes.say: What if gRPC didn't need H T T P slash two at all? This is grpc-over-datachannels: gRPC running over a single WebRTC data channel, in sixteen languages, with zero runtime dependencies.

scenes.heading: Why not HTTP/2?
bullets: Browsers cannot open raw TCP or serve HTTP/2 endpoints
Every language needs its own heavyweight gRPC stack
Reaching a peer behind NAT means servers and signaling
scenes.say: Stock gRPC assumes H T T P slash two and a reachable server endpoint. Browsers can't open raw T C P. Every language drags in its own heavyweight stack. And reaching a peer behind a NAT means standing up servers and signaling. There is a shorter path.

scenes.heading: One channel, many calls
bullets: A small frame protocol over one ordered RTCDataChannel
Unary, server-streaming, client-streaming, bidi — all multiplexed
Our own WebRTC stack: ICE, DTLS, SCTP, written from scratch
scenes.say: Instead, many concurrent calls are multiplexed onto one ordered, reliable data channel, using a small frame protocol. All four g R P C call shapes work. Underneath sits our own WebRTC stack: ICE, D T L S, and S C T P, rebuilt from scratch with no external dependencies.

scenes.heading: Generated runtimes, 16 languages
bullets: Rust, JavaScript, Go, Python, Java, C#, C++, Swift
Kotlin, Dart, Zig, C99, Lua, Ruby, PHP, Scala
Native clients and servers; browser clients incl. WASM facades
scenes.say: The runtimes are generated, not handwritten. One source of truth, expanded by recursive metaprogramming into runtimes and protoc plugins for sixteen languages. Native clients and servers, plus browser clients, including WASM facades that wrap the JavaScript client.

scenes.heading: Graded against stock gRPC
bullets: Oracle tests: generated wire vs Google/Java/Go implementations
TCP-to-DataChannel proxy puts reference gRPC on the same wire
Behaviour is checked against the reference, not just itself
scenes.say: Generated code is only trustworthy if something independent grades it. So generated tests run the wire protocol against stock gRPC implementations, bridged through a T C P to DataChannel proxy. Behaviour is checked against the reference, not just against itself.

scenes.heading: WebRTC-Direct: no signaling
bullets: Server prints one certhash multiaddr; client dials it
Direct UDP on LAN and public hosts
TURN relay for symmetric NAT; full ICE + STUN peer mode
scenes.say: The newest examples go further: WebRTC-Direct. A server listens on a U D P socket and prints one certhash multiaddr. A client dials that address and gets a data channel. No signaling server, no S D P exchange. Direct on a LAN, through a TURN relay behind symmetric NAT, or full ICE with STUN in peer mode.

scenes.heading: Live: direct echo, Node server to Node client
scenes.say: Here it is live. The server prints its multiaddr; the client dials it directly and the echo comes back over the data channel. Every other language does the same thing, natively or through the generated sidecar transport.

scenes.heading: Try it in your browser
scenes.say: You can try it right now: the in-browser generator turns your proto file into stubs and runtimes, entirely client-side. The code is on GitHub, with direct examples in every language. Links are in the description.
